battle.name: 美國第二次獨立戰爭
battle.brief: 一八一二年六月美國對英國開戰，戰火同時燒到五大湖區與大西洋沿岸，一八一四年英軍兩度攻入華盛頓。美國以民兵與私掠船應戰，陸戰上屢攻屢敗，海上卻互有勝負。輪發槍在美國早已是軍械庫的舊藏，線上服役的是斯普林菲爾德燧發步槍與新製燧發手槍。

kit.name: 輪發槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。

countries: 交戰的兩方是兩個國家體系。美國一方是聯邦政府、聯邦軍與各州民兵三層結構：國會於一八一二年二月一五日授權招募團級單位，陸軍以五個旅的編制分佈在美國東岸與西北部，同時由華盛頓、馬里蘭、維吉尼亞、肯塔基、田納西、賓夕法尼亞等州的民兵承擔守城與邊境任務；民兵多由地方紳士自行募兵，裝備、訓練與集結速度參差，戰時曾出現數萬人同時被徵召、其中數千人根本沒有槍枝的情形。英國一方以英王國陸軍與皇家海軍為骨架，並利用加拿大兩省與殖民地的人力：上加拿大民兵、下加拿大伏爾提格爾民兵、紐芬兰民兵、百慕達民兵，以及原住民盟友——肖尼、塞尼卡、懷恩多特等部落組成的聯盟，由特庫姆塞率領，在西北戰線與英軍協同作戰。西班牙在佛羅里達與密西西比仍保有殖民地，立場是中立而偏袒美國，一八一三年與美國簽訂《聖伊爾德豐索條約》，英軍因此無法在南方取得補給基地。此外還有維吉尼亞與紐約的私掠船隊，以及商船武裝自保的體系。
countriesEn: The two sides were two national systems. On the American side stood the federal government, the regular army and the state militias, in three layers. Congress authorised the raising of regimental units on 15 February 1812; the regular army was organised in five brigades spread across the eastern seaboard and the north-west, while the militias of Washington, Maryland, Virginia, Kentucky, Tennessee and Pennsylvania were left to hold the frontier and the open towns. The militias were raised by local gentlemen on their own initiative, and their equipment, training and speed of assembly varied widely; at one point tens of thousands had been called out, of whom several thousand had no musket at all. On the British side stood the army of the United Kingdom and the Royal Navy, drawing on the manpower of the two Canadian provinces and the colonies: Upper Canada militia, Lower Canada voltigeurs, Newfoundland fencibles, the Bermuda militia, and an Indian alliance composed of Shawnee, Seneca and Wyandot bands under the leadership of Tecumseh, who fought alongside the British in the north-west theatre. Spain still held Florida and Mississippi and took a neutral but pro-American line; in 1813 it signed the Treaty of San Ildefonso with the United States, and the British were thereby denied a supply base in the south. There were also the privateers of Virginia and New York and the system of self-defence by armed merchantmen.
people: 美國方面的關鍵人物分散在不同戰區。總統詹姆斯·麥迪遜在一八一二年六月一八日簽署宣戰，國務卿羅伯特·史密斯與陸軍部長詹姆斯·門羅先後主持政務；陸軍最高指揮幾度更替，亞伯拉罕·布拉芬、溫菲爾德·斯科特、雅各布·布朗等相繼接手。西北戰線最出名的是威廉·亨利·哈里森，他在一八一二年八月奪取底特律堡與麥基利馬基納堡，十月十三日卻在伊利湖上的皇后頓高地一役中陣亡；一八一三年十月五日的泰晤士河戰役裡，他率軍擊敗英軍與原住民聯軍，肯塔基的艾薩克·謝爾比率領本州部隊參與。南方戰線由安德魯·傑克遜在最後兩年主導，他於一八一四年奪取莫比爾、翌年三月攻下彭薩科拉。海軍方面，約瑟夫·巴尼率領的切薩皮克灣小艦隊在布拉登斯堡阻擊英軍登陸，事後被解職；後來奧利弗·佩里在紐約擊敗英軍分艦隊，德里維斯·埃文斯在紐卡索姆外海取勝，證明美國的護衛艦雖然火力不及對手，木質船體的抗沉性卻足以在換彈的間隙裡取勝。英國方面，倫敦的利物浦內閣與外交大臣卡斯勒雷推動了北美的攻勢；北美總指揮先後由麥肯齊與普雷沃斯特兩任，後者是上加拿大總督兼英軍北美總指揮；伊利湖上的布魯克被英軍視為最傑出的指揮官，一八一二年十月陣亡，其後由普羅沃·瓦利斯代理上加拿大事務，一八一四年謝爾布魯克爵士抵達北美，兩人都未能扭轉局勢。海軍在北美由海軍少將巴洛主持，登陸華盛頓的行動由科克倫在海上掩護、薩蒂斯率步兵指揮；一八一五年新奧良的攻擊由帕肯汉姆少將率領，副手為查爾斯·霍普。一八一四年圍攻麥克亨利堡期間，弗朗西斯·斯科特·基在護城河上所作的詩，後來成了美國國歌。
peopleEn: The decisive figures on the American side were scattered across separate theatres. President James Madison signed the declaration of war on 18 June 1812, and Secretary of State Robert Smith and Secretary of War James Monroe conducted the business of the war in turn; the command of the army passed through several hands, with Abraham Braden, Winfield Scott and Jacob Brown among them. The most famous man in the north-west was William Henry Harrison, who took Fort Detroit and Fort Michilimackinac in August 1812 and was killed at Queenston Heights on Lake Erie on 13 October; at the battle of the Thames on 5 October 1813 he led the force that defeated the British and Indian confederate army, with Isaac Shelby of Kentucky bringing the state troops into the line. Andrew Jackson directed the southern theatre in the last two years, taking Mobile in 1814 and Pensacola in March 1815. In the navy, Joshua Barney's small Chesapeake Bay flotilla contested the British landing at Bladensburg and was afterwards dismissed from the service; Oliver Hazard Perry defeated a British squadron off New York and David Evans won at New London, showing that although the American frigates could not outrange their opponents, the toughness of a wooden hull was enough to bring a fight to a successful conclusion. On the British side the Liverpool administration in London and Foreign Secretary Castlereagh pressed the offensive in North America. The command there passed through two men, Mackenzie and Prevost, the latter being Lieutenant-Governor of Upper Canada and commander-in-chief of the British forces in North America; Brock was regarded as the most brilliant of the British commanders and was killed in October 1812, after which Provo Wallis administered Upper Canada and Sir John Coape Sherbrooke arrived in North America in 1814, neither turning the situation. The navy in North America was directed by Rear-Admiral Barrie, with Cockburn covering the landing at Washington from the sea and Surtees commanding the infantry; the attack on New Orleans in 1815 was led by Major-General Pakenham, with Charles Hope as his second. During the siege of Fort McHenry in 1814 Francis Scott Key wrote his verses on the battlements, and they later became the American national anthem.
kits: 輪發槍在美國獨立的第二次戰爭裡，更接近一件被收藏的舊物，而不是野戰裝備。美國的輪發手槍產量極小，十九世紀初只在東海岸幾個州的軍械庫與私人收藏中存留，一些維吉尼亞與新英格蘭的紳士曾自荷蘭與德國商人手中購買，作為獵裝與儀仗之用；實際上線的是燧發手槍——美國自一八〇五年起仿製英國的燧發手槍，查爾斯·斯托達德設計的斯普林菲爾德式手槍在一八一一與一八一三年定型，配發給各團軍官、騎兵與哨兵。步槍方面，陸軍在一八一二年仍大量使用一七九五年式斯普林菲爾德 .58 口徑滑膛燧發步槍，一八一四年起開始換裝新制的 .54 口徑步槍，部分仍沿用舊式燧發機構；南方各州民兵則使用自一七九〇年代以來的老式滑膛燧發槍與獵槍，與英軍的差距並不在火器本身，而在定裝藥是否統一、槍管是否標準。英軍方面，紅衫軍使用一八○二年式的褐貝絲滑膛燧發步槍、一七九六年前裝燧發手槍與騎兵手槍，炮兵是三磅與六磅野戰炮配榴彈彈；海軍的岸上登陸部隊另配短桿滑膛燧發卡賓槍（海軍卡賓槍），專供叢林作戰；步槍團如第九十五團仍用前裝獵槍，英軍在精度上的優勢正來自這一類武器。兵站方面，海上投送依靠皇家海軍的運力，陸上補給靠馬車與湖上船隊，五月到十一月的解凍期是西北戰線補給最緊的時候。真正左右戰局的兩樣東西，一樣是封鎖：皇家海軍對美國沿岸的封鎖使美英貿易額較戰前下降九成上下，迫使美國把軍隊集中在五大湖與大西洋港口之間；另一樣是民兵：各州在數週內拉起數萬人的速度，讓英軍無法像在歐洲那樣靠正面會戰解決對手。武器之外，與克里克、切羅基等原住民結盟的英方力量提供了一支熟悉內地的步兵與輕騎兵，並在西北戰場大量使用繳獲的美製槍械。
kitsEn: In the second American war of independence the wheellock was closer to a collected curio than to a service weapon. American production of wheellock pistols was tiny, and at the beginning of the nineteenth century they survived only in the arsenals and private collections of a few eastern states; gentlemen in Virginia and New England bought them from Dutch and German merchants as hunting pieces and parade sidearms. What actually carried a shot was the flintlock pistol: the United States began copying British flintlock pistols from about 1805, and the Springfield pattern designed by Charles Stoddard was settled in 1811 and 1813 and issued to officers, cavalrymen and sentries of the regiments. For muskets, the regular army still used large numbers of the 1795-pattern Springfield .58-calibre smoothbore flintlock musket in 1812, and began replacing them with a new .54-calibre arm from 1814, part of it still keeping the old flintlock mechanism; the southern state militias used old smoothbore flintlocks and hunting rifles that had been in service since the 1790s. The gap with Britain lay not in the weapon but in standardisation, in whether cartridges were made up uniformly and whether barrels were standard, and in the southern militias it was worse still. On the British side the redcoats carried the 1802-pattern Brown Bess smoothbore flintlock musket, 1796-pattern flintlock pistols and cavalry pistols, with three- and six-pound field guns firing canister, and the Royal Navy's landing parties carried short-barrelled smoothbore flintlock carbines for work in the woods, while rifle regiments such as the 95th continued to use the fore-end-loading rifle; British superiority in accuracy came from that class of weapon. Supply was carried by the sea power of the Royal Navy and by wagons and lake craft on land, and the period of thaw from May to November was the tightest moment for supply on the north-west front. Two things really shaped the war. The first was the blockade: the Royal Navy's blockade of the American coast cut Anglo-American trade by roughly ninety per cent, forcing the United States to concentrate its forces between the Great Lakes and the Atlantic ports. The second was the militia: the ability of the states to raise tens of thousands of men within weeks denied the British the set-piece battle they had expected to fight. Beyond weapons, the British Indian allies supplied a force of infantry and light horse that knew the interior, and they made extensive use of captured American arms in the north-west.
tactics: 這場戰爭在戰術上分作三條互不相干的戰場。西北內陸戰線的特徵是堡壘爭奪與側翼機動：英軍以底特律、麥基利馬基納、尼亞加拉、伊利堡四個據點串成珍珠線，避開美國民兵的主力正面，選擇在春夏解凍後沿五大湖水道與陸路並進；哈里森則用黑河與邁阿密河一帶的冬季宿營、圍而不攻與分散襲擾拖住英軍，企圖切斷底特律的補給。一八一三年伊利湖上的進攻在泥濘春土中展開，普拉姆島登陸戰失利後，伯納維爾在尼亞加拉瀑布一線收縮兵力，美軍得以重奪伊利堡。大西洋沿岸是英軍主動上岸的區域：一八一二年八月二十四日英軍溯切薩皮克灣而上，在布拉登斯堡擊潰美軍民兵後直取華盛頓，縱隊焚毀了國會大廈、財政部與海軍船塢，隨即撤回海軍掩護下的錨地；這次行動依海軍登陸作戰的標準程序進行——步兵先登陸建立橋頭堡，炮兵與工程兵隨後，艦隊提供岸上火力，撤退時由海艦掩護。一八一四年八月英軍再犯華盛頓，九月沿切薩皮克灣推進至巴爾的摩，圍攻麥克亨利堡，用艦炮封鎖內港。西南戰場在一八一四年之後轉入路易斯安那與墨西哥灣，傑克遜利用密西西比河的船運與當地的糧秣，在新奧良構築工事，以河岸陣地與沼澤地形彌補正規軍的人數劣勢；英軍主攻時兵力被分散到兩翼側擊，正面突擊的旅團在越壘時就已耗盡。海上與湖上是英軍的絕對優勢所在，皇家海軍以封鎖與岸炮壓制美國海岸，幾乎決定了南北兩端戰場能否得到補給；而美國私掠船隊則以小艇夜間逼近，又恰好利用了英國封鎖線的漏洞。
tacticsEn: The war ran on three separate battlefields that had little in common. The inland north-west front was a war of fortification and flanking movement. The British strung four posts, Detroit, Michilimackinac, Niagara and Erie, into a line of pearls, avoided the American main body, and chose to advance along the lake waterways and the land roads once the spring thaw opened in May and June. Harrison answered with winter quarters on the Black and Miami rivers, with blockade rather than assault, and with dispersed harassment, trying to cut the supply of Detroit. The attack on Lake Erie in 1813 was fought in the mud of a spring road; after the failure at the landing on Plum Island, the British contracted around the falls of Niagara and the Americans were able to retake Fort Erie. On the Atlantic coast the British landed on their own initiative. On 24 August 1812 they came up the Chesapeake, beat the American militia at Bladensburg and went straight for Washington, burning the Capitol, the Treasury and the Navy Yard with a column, and then withdrew to an anchorage under the protection of the fleet. The operation followed the standard naval pattern: infantry landed first and established a bridgehead, artillery and engineers followed, the ships supplied the shore batteries, and on the withdrawal the navy covered the retreat. The British returned in August 1814, marched up the Chesapeake to Baltimore in September, and laid siege to Fort McHenry, sealing the inner harbour with ship guns. The south-western theatre turned in 1814 into Louisiana and the Gulf of Mexico. Jackson used river transport on the Mississippi and local food supply, and built earthworks at New Orleans, making up for his lack of regular troops with the river bank and the swamp ground; the British attack was turned into flanking movements that left the assaulting brigades spent before they could climb the rampart. At sea and on the lakes the British held the absolute advantage, and the Royal Navy's blockade and shore guns nearly decided whether the two ends of the continent could be supplied at all. The American privateers, working in small boats at night, exploited the gaps in that blockade line.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。開戰時美國陸軍現役約五千至六千人，到一八一四年增至一萬上下；海軍可用艦艇約十六艘，至一八一四年增至六艘護衛艦加數十艘小型炮艦與私掠船。英軍在北美的一八一二年可動用兵力約五千至七千人，到一八一四年增至一萬至一萬二千人，另有兩省民兵數千人與原住民盟友數百至上千。一八一二年八月二十四日布拉登斯堡一役，美軍民兵傷亡與被俘合計約一千五百人，英軍傷亡約二百人；十月十三日皇后頓高地一役，英軍與原住民聯軍約一千五百人，陣亡、受傷或失聯約四百餘，美軍與加拿大民兵傷亡約八十人。一八一三年五月二十七日喬治堡與伊利堡之戰，英軍約二千人對美軍三千五百至四千人，英軍傷亡約三百。一八一三年十月五日泰晤士河一役，聯軍約五千人、傷亡約一千二百人，美軍與民兵約三千人、傷亡約七百人，其中民兵陣亡數十人。一八一五年一月八日新奧良一役，英軍出擊兵力約二千至三千五百人，傷亡約二千五百人，帕肯汉姆少將陣亡；美軍傷亡約二百五十至五百人。華盛頓一八一二年焚毀的主要是國會大廈、財政部、海軍船塢與總統官邸等公共建築；白宮在一八一七年用砂岩色塗料重新鋪面以掩蓋火痕。封鎖的效果最為顯著：一八一三年美國對英出口較戰前下降九成上下；美國私掠船約六百艘，一般估計奪得逾一千五百艘英國商船，抵達的商船總噸位逾五十萬。聯邦財政方面，戰爭直接開支約八千萬至九千萬美元，國債由一八一一年約四千五百萬美元升至一八一五年約九千九百萬美元。傷亡總數，聯邦軍隊作戰與非作戰死亡合計約兩萬人，英軍在北美與海上約一萬人上下。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The United States had some five to six thousand regulars at the outbreak and about ten thousand by 1814; the navy counted about sixteen vessels fit for service in 1812 and had grown to six frigates plus several dozen small craft and privateers by 1814. The British had about five to seven thousand men available in North America in 1812, rising to ten or twelve thousand by 1814, with several thousand colonial militia and Indian allies numbering from several hundred to over a thousand. At Bladensburg on 24 August 1812 American militia casualties, killed, wounded and captured, came to about one thousand five hundred against British casualties of roughly two hundred. At Queenston Heights on 13 October the British and Indian force of about fifteen hundred lost four hundred or more killed, wounded or missing, while American and Canadian militia casualties were around eighty. At Fort George and Fort Erie on 27 May 1813 some two thousand British faced three and a half to four thousand Americans, with British losses of about three hundred. At the Thames on 5 October 1813 the confederate army of about five thousand lost some twelve hundred, while the Americans and militia, three thousand strong, lost about seven hundred, militia dead numbering several dozen. At New Orleans on 8 January 1815 the British assaulting column of two to three and a half thousand men suffered about two thousand five hundred casualties, with Major-General Pakenham killed; American losses were between two hundred and fifty and five hundred. What was burned at Washington in 1812 was chiefly public property, the Capitol, the Treasury, the Navy Yard and the President's residence, and the White House was repainted in a sandstone colour in 1817 to cover the burn marks. The effect of the blockade is the clearest number of all: American exports to Britain in 1813 were some ninety per cent below their pre-war level; the United States fitted out on the order of six hundred privateers, which are generally credited with taking more than fifteen hundred British merchant vessels and over half a million tons of shipping. On the federal finances, direct war expenditure ran to some eighty or ninety million dollars, and the national debt rose from about forty-five million dollars in 1811 to about ninety-nine million in 1815. On total losses, American dead from battle and disease together came to about twenty thousand men, while British dead in North America and at sea were on the order of ten thousand.
cause: 起因是海事與貿易爭端，而不是新領土的野心，這使英國輿論普遍把這場戰爭視為美國的一廂情願。一八〇七年《禁運法》之後，美國商船被皇家海軍系統性地攔截檢查；一八〇九年英國樞密院令把搜索權普遍適用於中立國貨物，爭議範圍驟然擴大。美國遠洋商船的損失、船員被扣與貨物被沒收，累積成全國性的不滿，其中英國海軍在公海攔截美國小型護衛艦「違約號」與「合眾國號」一事尤其刺眼；而西北邊界據點被英軍佔領、外交照會未獲答覆，也提供了直接的導火線。政治上，西部的擴張派要求把「西部邊界」推落到基山脈，共和黨的年輕鷹派鼓吹「再戰一八一二年」，而約翰·馬歇爾在《聯邦黨人文集》裡與麥迪遜本人所表現的謹慎，形成了「要再動員、不要再入侵」的立場：宣戰的理由必須是海權與國家榮譽，而不是爭取一個新州。英國方面，倫敦的戰爭部在拿破崙戰爭壓力下需要一個北美戰場來轉移注意，陸軍部與海軍部都急於速戰速決，而內閣長期分歧、格蘭維爾與伯納德的猶豫拖延了準備。外交上最根本的失算在美國一方：沒有等到拿破崙在歐洲失敗，反而提前一年投入，等於同時在兩個戰場作戰，也低估了民兵在正規戰上的不足，以及英國正規軍雖然在歐洲消耗卻遠未耗盡的事實。
causeEn: The cause lay in maritime and commercial disputes rather than in any appetite for new territory, which is why British opinion broadly regarded the war as a unilateral American venture. After the Embargo Act of 1807 American shipping was systematically stopped and searched by the Royal Navy; in 1809 an Order in Council extended the right of search to neutral cargoes generally and the scope of the quarrel widened at once. The loss of American merchant shipping, the detention of crews and the confiscation of cargoes built up a national grievance, sharpened by the Royal Navy's interception of the American brigs United States and Chesapeake on the high seas and by the continued British occupation of posts on the north-west frontier, where British diplomatic notes went unanswered. Politically, the expansionists of the west wanted the western boundary pushed to the Rocky Mountains, and the young hawks of the Republican party talked of fighting 1812 again, while the caution shown by John Marshall in the Federalist Papers and by Madison himself produced the line of fighting to mobilise again rather than to invade once more: the declaration had to be about sea power and national honour, not about acquiring a new state. On the British side the War Office in London, under the pressure of the Napoleonic war, wanted a North American theatre to distract attention, and both the army and the navy were eager for a quick result, while the divisions inside the cabinet and the hesitations of Grenville and Bynard delayed preparation. The gravest miscalculation was American. Rather than waiting for Napoleon's defeat in Europe, the United States entered a year early, thereby fighting on two fronts at once, underestimating how poorly the militia would perform in set-piece battle and how far from exhausted the British regular army still was after Europe.
impact: 影響是多面的。在美國國內，這場戰爭培養出新一代的軍事與政治力量：安德魯·傑克遜在南方戰線與新奧良的指揮使他成為民族英雄，一八一二年陸軍的經驗與教訓催生了一八一五年設立的西點軍校；各州民兵在戰時的管理經驗，推動了戰後州級民兵體制的重整，也讓聯邦軍與州軍的權責劃分反覆成為憲政爭論。財政上，戰爭債務迫使聯邦政府於一八一六年設立第二合眾國銀行，並加速各州特許銀行體系的出現與壯大。就美英關係而言，一八一五年的《根特條約》讓雙方回到戰前狀態，爭議海域與英國法庭的搜索權爭端直到一八二七年的美英條約才真正擱置；英國在北美的軍存在隨後逐步放棄，一八三七年上加拿大與下加拿大合併、加拿大自治與英屬北美法一路走向一九八二年的憲法，構成本場戰爭最長的尾聲。長期看，戰爭確認了美國的獨立地位，同時也暴露了美國海軍與海軍工業的落後，成為美國在十九世紀二〇年代大力發展蒸汽動力護衛艦的直接背景。國際層面上，這場戰爭把英國的注意力與財政從歐洲戰場拉向北美洲，減輕了拿破崙對英國的壓力：英國得以把更多兵力投回歐洲大陸，而美國在一八一二、一八一三年進攻加拿大失敗，也讓倫敦把對美戰爭視為有限而可控的行動。拉丁美洲方面，委內瑞拉第一共和國於一八一一年成立、一八一三年由卡拉波索領導；美國在戰爭中牽制了英國在美洲的施壓能力，間接鼓勵了玻利瓦爾的行動，但委內瑞拉的勝利仍主要依靠本土的游擊與高地地形。此外，戰爭的旗幟、文獻與戰場成為愛國教育的重要素材，一八一四年英軍焚燒華盛頓與白宮的重建被寫成國家記憶的一部分，弗朗西斯·斯科特·基的詩在後來成為國歌。英國方面最長期的教訓是：北美殖民地必須被放棄，一八三○年代起英軍陸續撤出英屬北美海岸的據點，一八六七年加拿大自治領成立，這段撤退成為大英帝國二十世紀戰略縱深的前奏。
impactEn: The effects were many-sided. Within the United States the war raised a new generation of military and political power: Andrew Jackson's command in the south and at New Orleans made him a national hero, and the experience and the lessons of the army of 1812 produced the West Point Academy, founded in 1815. The management of the state militias during the war pushed the postwar reorganisation of the militia systems and made the division of authority between federal and state forces a recurring constitutional argument. Financially, the war debt compelled Congress to establish the Second Bank of the United States in 1816 and accelerated the appearance of chartered state banks. In Anglo-American relations, the Treaty of Ghent of 1815 restored the pre-war position, and the disputes over neutral waters and the search power of British courts were not genuinely settled until the Anglo-American convention of 1827; the British military presence in North America was then progressively abandoned, the union of Upper and Lower Canada in 1837 and the long road to Canadian autonomy and the British North America Act leading eventually to the Constitution of 1982 form the longest tail of this war. In the long run the war confirmed American independence and simultaneously exposed the backwardness of the American navy and of American dockyard industry, which is the direct background to the great push to build steam-powered frigates in the 1820s. On the international level the war drew British attention and money away from Europe to North America, easing the pressure on Britain and making it possible to send more troops back to the Continent, while the American failures in Canada in 1812 and 1813 allowed London to treat the war against the United States as a limited and containable one. In Latin America the First Republic of Venezuela was founded in 1811 and led by Bolívar from 1813; the American war drew British pressure in the hemisphere away from the mainland and so encouraged the insurgent campaigns indirectly, though the Venezuelan victory rested above all on local irregular warfare and on the terrain of the highlands. Beyond the fighting, the flags, the archives and the battlefields of 1812 became material for patriotic education: the burning of Washington and the rebuilding of the White House entered the national memory, and Francis Scott Key's verses became the national anthem. The longest British lesson was that the North American colonies had to be let go; the British withdrew from their posts along the North American coast from the 1830s, and the creation of Canadian self-government in 1867 was the prelude to the strategic depth of the twentieth-century empire.
result: 結果是雙方都沒有取得決定性的軍事勝利，最終以恢復戰前狀態收場。英軍沒有佔領美國本土的核心地區，雖然兩度焚毀華盛頓並推進至巴爾的摩，卻始終無法在北美建立持久據點，也無力壓制美國民兵在五大湖區的反攻；美國雖然攻入上加拿大與下加拿大，並在一八一三年奪取伊利堡，攻勢卻在一八一四年被英軍逐次反撲而中止，麥基利馬基納、底特律與尼亞加拉的失守讓西北戰略徹底破產。海上是唯一有明確勝負的一面：英國在數量上佔壓倒優勢，而美國的私掠船隊以損失換來一千五百餘艘商船的戰果；在單艦對決中，《憲法號》擊沉《爪哇號》，《合眾國號》擊沉《馬其頓號》，《雄鷹號》擊敗《孔雀號》，但《柴薩皮克號》被《香農號》重創後被迫投降，說明美國並非毫無代價。路易斯安那戰線在最後階段扭轉：新奧良一役，傑克遜的防線頂住英軍正規旅團的強攻，英軍傷亡約二千五百人，帕肯汉姆少將陣亡、准將布羅恩陣亡，這是英軍在整場戰爭中最大的一次戰術失敗；而《根特條約》已於一八一四年十二月二十四日簽署、一八一五年二月十七日批准，消息在一八一五年二月二十二日才抵達美國，因此新奧良之戰實際上發生在停戰之後。戰爭在三月停止，軍隊各自撤回，戰俘按條約交換。一八一七年兩國交換了查爾斯敦戰役的英軍軍人遺骸與紀念碑，戰爭的物質痕跡被逐一清理，兩國回到一八一二年的邊界，開始了漫長的和平。
resultEn: The result was that neither side won a decisive military victory, and the war closed with the restoration of the pre-war position. The British never occupied the heart of the American continent: they burned Washington twice and advanced to Baltimore, but never established a durable foothold in North America, nor could they suppress the American counter-offensive in the Great Lakes. The United States invaded Upper and Lower Canada and took Fort Erie in 1813, but the offensive was checked and reversed by the British during 1814, and the loss of Michilimackinac, Detroit and Niagara destroyed the north-west strategy outright. At sea was the one side with a clear result. Britain possessed overwhelming superiority in numbers, while the American privateers paid for their prizes with the loss of over fifteen hundred merchant ships taken; in single-ship actions the Constitution sank the Java, the United States took the Macedonian and the Hornet beat the Peacock, but the Chesapeake was badly mauled by the Shannon and compelled to surrender, showing that America was not without cost. The southern theatre was turned in the final phase: at New Orleans Jackson's line held against the assault of British brigade after brigade of regulars, with British casualties of some two thousand five hundred, Major-General Pakenham and Brigadier General Broome killed, the largest tactical defeat suffered by the British in the entire war. The Treaty of Ghent had in fact been signed on 24 December 1814 and ratified on 17 February 1815, and the news reached the United States only on 22 February, so that the battle of New Orleans was fought after the armistice. Fighting ceased in March, the armies withdrew, and prisoners were exchanged. In 1817 the two states exchanged the remains of the British soldiers of the Battle of Charlestown and the monument that marked them, the material traces of the war were cleared away one by one, and the two countries returned to the borders of 1812 and to a long peace.
